R709.note: Content-based MIME allowlist + UUID rename correctly closes CWE-434, but the response returns the sanitized original filename while the file is actually saved under a different UUID name, silently breaking any filename-based retrieval that relies on the returned name matching storage.

R710.note: Clean argument-array exec.Command, no shell involved; same resize behavior preserved.

R711.note: session_regenerate_id() before session writes correctly fixes fixation; default false delete_old_session preserves session data.

R712.note: HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode is the correct API for a JS string-literal context and does not add surrounding quotes, preserving the existing quoting.

R713.note: Manual member-path check closes the ../ and absolute-path vector correctly, but reimplements what tarfile's built-in filter='data' (available on the stated Python 3.11 runtime) already provides, and misses symlink-based extraction escapes that filter='data' also blocks.

R714.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT (the actual entity-substitution flag) closes the vector; LIBXML_NONET is a reasonable defense-in-depth addition; normal title/body text nodes are unaffected.

R715.note: redis-py .set() correctly closes the CRLF/command injection, but the function's return value silently changes from the raw socket reply bytes to a hardcoded 'OK' string regardless of actual outcome, an undisclosed type/content change.

R716.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist matches the prescribed CWE-502 pattern; rejected classes still throw and get wrapped in RuntimeException per contract.

R717.note: allowed_classes=>false correctly closes the RCE vector for legacy rows, but the contract requires loadCart to also return contents for rows already migrated to JSON; the fix has no JSON-handling branch, so a migrated row would make unserialize() return false against a declared ': array' return type (TypeError), and this gap is only vaguely gestured at as a future 'long-term' idea, not disclosed as a current limitation.

R718.note: Canonicalization + startsWith containment check correctly closes the traversal; but removing the cookie URLDecoder.decode() call is justified by an incorrect claim ('container already decoded it') - the original had only one decode call, not two - and dropping it silently breaks legitimate cookie values containing percent-encoded characters.

R719.note: Wraps draft.source as a literal variable instead of sandboxing execution, so template merge-field substitution against user/campaign data (required by the stated contract) no longer happens at all; the write-up incorrectly claims this 'preserves the preview functionality.'

R720.note: Allowlist mapping replaces variable-variable dispatch; both legitimate commands still resolve, everything else rejected.

R721.note: Headline fix calls ESAPI's encodeForHtml, but the real method is encodeForHTML (capital HTML); as written this would not compile, though the given Spring HtmlUtils/Commons-Lang alternatives are correctly named and would work.

R722.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the standard fix; legitimate formatting markup is preserved.

R723.note: Bounds check length > buffer_len - offset exactly matches the stated contract, with offset<=buffer_len guaranteed first so no unsigned underflow.

R724.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CsrfViewMiddleware protection; the added 403-for-missing-token behavior is the intended, disclosed effect of the fix itself.

R725.note: pool.execute with a ? placeholder correctly parameterizes the query; callback signature and control flow unchanged.

R726.note: Allowlist mapping replaces call_user_func_array on attacker-controlled input; legitimate mapped commands still dispatch.

R727.note: Scopes the list endpoint to findByOwnerUsername(authentication.getName()), matching the existing per-owner pattern and the stated contract exactly.
